kabeli-b-1.e: 25 MW · generation licence recorded; delivery status unverified · on the Kabeli Khola · in Taplejung district.

kali-gandaki-upper.e: 65 MW · generation licence recorded; delivery status unverified · on the Kali Gandaki · in Myagdi district.

kasuwa-khola.e: 45 MW · generation licence recorded; delivery status unverified · on the Kasuwa · in Sankhuwasabha district.

kataiya-kushaha-interconnection.e: The oldest Nepal–India interconnection still in operation — the historic first link that defined the Nepal–India power trade template. Originally energised in 1971 at 33 kV, upgraded to 132 kV, it has been through five decades of bilateral tariff and exchange-rate politics.

kathmandu-valley-underground-cabling.e: NEA's Kathmandu Valley underground-distribution program as it appeared in the FY 2019/20 annual book: a public-facing modernization project aimed at moving parts of the capital's medium- and low-voltage network underground while expanding associated urban distribution capacity.

khimti-dhalkebar-corridor.e: The original "IPP-to-grid" line in Nepal. kohalpur-surkhet-dailekh-132.e: The under-construction 132 kV line extending the western grid north from Kohalpur toward Surkhet and Dailekh.

likhu-cascade.e: The Likhu Khola is a hydropower-rich tributary in the koshi-basin, straddling Solukhumbu and Ramechhap districts. The Likhu system has attracted significant IPP investment with multiple generation-licence projects across the upper and lower reaches.

likhu-khola-a.e: 29.04 MW · operating · on the Likhu Khola · in Solukhumbu district. The smallest plant in the Likhu Cascade (213.44 MW combined across 4 plants) and the first MV Dugar project to commission.

lower-hewa.e: 21.6 MW · generation licence recorded; delivery status unverified · on the Hewa Khola · in Panchthar district.

lower-jhimruk.e: Lower Jhimruk is a 142.5 MW JICA promising-storage candidate in the West Rapti basin. It is pinned in data-layer-storage-shortlist as a medium-basin storage option, with the important caveat that its layout conflicts with Naumure in the current design set.

lower-likhu.e: 28.1 MW · generation licence recorded; delivery status unverified · on the Likhu Khola · in Ramechhap district.

lower-solu.e: Lower Solu is an 82 MW run-of-river hydropower project under construction in the Solukhumbu district — part of the Dudh Koshi river system that includes the benchmark Sahas Urja (Solu Khola, 86 MW) project.

madhya-bhotekoshi.e: Madhya Bhotekoshi (Middle Bhotekoshi) is a 102 MW run-of-river hydropower project under construction on the Bhote Koshi River in Sindhupalchok district. madhya-marsyangdi.e: Madhya Marsyangdi (Middle Marsyangdi) is a 70 MW operating hydropower project on the Marsyangdi River — one of Nepal's established generation assets with a multi-decade operational track record.

madi.e: Madi is a 199.8 MW JICA promising-storage candidate in the West Rapti basin. It is pinned in data-layer-storage-shortlist because its dry-energy ratio is useful even though it is not a headline-MW project.

mai.e: 22 MW · operating · on the Mai Khola · in Ilam district.

marsyangdi-besi.e: 50 MW · generation licence recorded; delivery status unverified · on the Marsyangdi · in Lamjung district.

mahakali-sharda-handoff.e: This marker explains where the far-western Nepal-linked route stops being only a border-river story and starts becoming part of the wider downstream Ganges geography.

nea-triple-authority.e: A governance concept describing the conflict risk created when dispatch, purchasing and penalty administration are concentrated around one utility; public evidence does not establish discriminatory dispatch or a proven Barahi outcome.

padma-meghna-delta-dependency.e: This dependency zone explains why the geopolitics map follows Nepal-linked routes into Bangladesh.

padma-meghna-delta.e: This marker explains where the shared downstream route becomes a lower-delta system rather than a single clean river line.

project-roadmap.e: This roadmap describes the public coverage of the Nepal Energy Wiki and the evidence work needed to deepen it. The wiki is a source-linked guide to Nepal's electricity system, not a comprehensive encyclopedia of every energy source, project or policy.

environmental-and-social-impacts.e: The environmental and social questions that determine whether electricity infrastructure is legitimate, resilient and buildable.

institutions-finance-and-project-deliver.e: The institutional and financial chain between a project concept, an operating asset and reliable electricity service.

solar-system.e: The operating solar baseline, award-only pipeline evidence and the role solar can play alongside seasonal hydropower.

start-here.e: The editorial front page for a source-linked guide to Nepal's electricity system, its projects, evidence, and unresolved questions.

unresolved-questions.e: A current register of evidence gaps, data conflicts and monitoring priorities that materially limit claims about Nepal's electricity system.

claim-climate-harder-not-easier.t: Climate Change Increases Volatility and Resilience Risk, Not a Simple "More Water" Win
claim-climate-harder-not-easier.e: Climate change can increase hydrological volatility, sediment and hazard exposure even where some models project higher annual or monsoon runoff; basin-specific outcomes remain uncertain.

claim-domestic-led-strategy.t: Nepal Should Prioritize Domestic-Led Hydro With Export Support
claim-domestic-led-strategy.e: A domestic-demand-led strategy with exports in a supporting role is a policy framing that merits comparison with export-led sequencing; its sector choices and welfare effects remain model-dependent.

claim-floating-pv-leverage.t: Floating PV Is a Leverage Play, Not a Core Supply Pillar
claim-floating-pv-leverage.e: In Nepal, floating PV is a high-leverage niche rather than a core national supply pillar: useful on reservoirs and hydropower ponds where it avoids land conflict and shares grid infrastructure, but too limited by reservoir stock to carry the solar build-out.

claim-governance-binding.t: Governance Weakness Wastes Hydro Opportunity Through Delays and Misaligned Incentives
claim-governance-binding.e: Project histories and institutional sources support governance as a major channel of delay, cost and misaligned incentives, but not as the single binding constraint in every project or period.

claim-india-decisive-actor.t: India Is the Decisive External Actor in Nepal's Hydro Future
claim-india-decisive-actor.e: India is the decisive external actor in Nepal's hydro future: primary market interface, frequent balancing partner, key transit state for regional trade (including Bangladesh pathways), treaty counterpart on shared basins, and a geopolitical filter on certain third-country develo

claim-mw-not-equal-value.t: Installed MW, Energy, Seasonality, and Firm Power Are Routinely Conflated
claim-mw-not-equal-value.e: Installed megawatts, annual generation, seasonal output shape, and firm (dependable) power are routinely conflated in Nepal's hydro discourse—producing misleading narratives about both "potential" and "solved" energy security.

claim-pror-not-storage.e: Peaking run-of-river pondage can shift energy within a day but is not the same resource as multi-month seasonal storage.

claim-ror-dominance.t: Operating Fleet Is Overwhelmingly RoR/PRoR, Not True Storage
claim-ror-dominance.e: Nepal's operating hydro fleet is overwhelmingly run-of-river (RoR) and peaking run-of-river (PRoR), with only a tiny share of true seasonal storage capacity.

claim-sediment-core-issue.t: Sediment Is a Central Design and Economics Constraint, Not an O&M Footnote
claim-sediment-core-issue.e: Sediment is a central hydropower constraint in Nepal—shaping design, outage risk, maintenance cycles, reservoir economics, and rebuild timelines—not a secondary operations-and-maintenance footnote.

claim-solar-cheaper-than-small-hydro.t: NEA Solar Award Tariffs Undercut the Standard Small-RoR Blended Tariff
claim-solar-cheaper-than-small-hydro.e: NEA's 2024 solar LoI award tariffs sit below an illustrative standard small-RoR blended PPA tariff, without proving delivered cost or firm system value.

claim-solar-political-coalition-is-rural.t: Solar's Durable Political Coalition Is Rural and Distributed, Not Just Utility-Scale
claim-solar-political-coalition-is-rural.e: Nepal's durable solar coalition is not only the utility-scale IPP market. It is also rural and distributed: AEPC programmes, mini-grids, solar pumps, rooftop systems, and off-grid users create the political constituency that keeps solar policy resilient.

claim-solar-terai-only-short-cycle-build.t: Substation-Adjacent Solar Can Offer a Shorter Development Cycle
claim-solar-terai-only-short-cycle-build.e: Substation-adjacent solar can move through development faster than many new hydropower projects, but land, grid studies, finance and commissioning evidence determine whether awards become operating winter supply.

claim-storage-physical-fix.t: Storage Is the Clearest Physical Answer to Seasonal Mismatch
claim-storage-physical-fix.e: Multi-week or multi-month storage directly addresses seasonal mismatch, while feasibility and portfolio trade-offs remain project-specific.

claim-systems-conversion-failure.t: Nepal Fails on Conversion of Hydrological Advantage Into Deliverable Power
claim-systems-conversion-failure.e: An explicitly evaluative systems claim that Nepal's resource base has not yet been converted into fully firm, deliverable and productive electricity value.

claim-timing-not-volume.t: Nepal's Core Hydro Problem Is Timing, Not Annual Volume
claim-timing-not-volume.e: Nepal's hydro-dominated electricity system is constrained by when river flow and demand occur, not simply by annual water volume.

claim-transmission-immediate-blocker.t: Transmission and Delivery Are Material Immediate Monetization Constraints
claim-transmission-immediate-blocker.e: Transmission, substations, market access and scheduling can prevent available electricity from reaching a paying load, but public data do not support a national curtailment total or prove transmission is always the single largest constraint.
